Chapter 11. The Law of the Inner Circle: Surrounding Yourself with the Right People
You know, no leader truly makes it on their own. The folks closest to you—your inner circle—can make all the difference in how effective you are and the kind of legacy you leave behind.
Picking the right people to stand beside you? That’s both a special privilege and a real responsibility.
Now, your inner circle isn’t just about having friends or loyal supporters. It’s really about building a team of people who bring their own unique strengths, fresh perspectives, and a deep commitment to your shared mission. These are the folks who won’t just pat you on the back—they’ll challenge you, support you, and hold you accountable when it matters most.
Think of it like a ship’s crew. Every crew member plays a specific part, and the entire journey hinges on how well they work together. A wise captain? They don’t just pick anyone—they choose people who are skilled, trustworthy, and truly believe in where the ship is headed.
So, how do you build a strong inner circle? Here are a few things that make a real difference.
First, you’ve got to spot and develop talent. Look for people who not only have potential, but also integrity. Investing in these folks pays off for everyone.
Then, encourage honest feedback and healthy debate. You want people around you who feel comfortable sharing different viewpoints—even when it’s a little uncomfortable.
And don’t forget about trust and respect. The best teams are built on relationships shaped by shared values and mutual respect.
Here’s a real-world example. Imagine a business owner who surrounds themselves with advisors willing to tell the truth, even when it’s hard to hear. That kind of openness leads to better decisions and helps avoid blind spots. On the flip side, leaders who cut themselves off or settle for mediocrity in their inner circle? They usually end up stuck or, even worse, heading toward failure.
The thing is, your inner circle isn’t set in stone. As your needs evolve, you might bring in new people, while others may move on. The key is being intentional—keep nurturing and renewing those relationships, so your team stays strong, connected, and moving in the right direction.
